S1.title: Wikipedia EN, History of Marseille
S1.quote: established within modern Marseille around 600 BC; c. 540 BC second wave of colonists; 49 BC Caesar's siege, the city fell by September; 5th c. Visigoths; 736-739 Umayyad forces invited in, Charles Martel sacks the city in 739; 1348 Black Death kills about 15,000 of 25,000; 1792 volunteers march to Paris; 1793 renamed Ville-sans-nom; 1869 Suez Canal; 22 Jan 1943 Action Tiger; Nov 1942-Aug 1944 German occupation

S2.title: Wikipedia EN, Timeline of Marseille
S2.quote: paraphrase: 470 taken by Visigoths under Euric; 839 sacked by Saracens; 1214 republic; 1252 taken by Charles of Anjou; 1262 revolt; 1423 sacked by Alfonso V; 1481 united with Provence; 1486 part of France; 1524 besieged; 1660 Louis XIV conquest, Forts Saint-Jean and Saint-Nicolas built; 1673 Hotel de Ville; 1720-21 plague; 1848 Paris-Marseille railway, Gare Saint-Charles; 1849 Canal de Marseille; 1853 La Joliette dock; 1864 Rue de la Republique opens; 1869 Palais Longchamp; 1906/1922 colonial exhibitions; 1937 Stade Velodrome; 1940 bombing; 1952 Cite radieuse; 2013 MuCEM

S3.title: Wikipedia EN, Siege of Massilia
S3.quote: paraphrase: 19 April to 6 September 49 BC; Caesarian victory and Roman annexation of Massilia; Brutus's fleet won at Tauroento on 31 July 49 BC

S4.title: Wikipedia EN, Incorporation of Provence into France
S4.quote: Charles III bequeathed Provence to Louis XI and died in December 1481; Estates of Provence approve union in 1482; perpetual union granted in letters patent of October 1486

S5.title: Wikipedia EN, Provence
S5.quote: paraphrase: 480 Visigoths enter Provence; 879 Boso first ruler of independent Provence; 1032 Provence a fiefdom of the Holy Roman Empire until 1246; 1112 Barcelona rule begins; 1246 Angevin rule begins; 1481 title passes to Louis XI; 1486 incorporated into the French royal domain

S6.title: Wikipedia FR, Rafle de Marseille
S6.quote: paraphrase: rafle on 22, 23 and 24 January 1943; German engineers dynamite from 1 February 1943; about 1,500 buildings and 14 hectares destroyed; 82 streets and squares and 850 shops disappeared; about 20,000 people rounded up; Hotel de ville, Hotel de Cabre, Maison Diamantee and Eglise Saint-Laurent spared; reconstruction of the Vieux-Port area not complete until 1956

S7.title: Wikipedia EN, Marseille roundup
S7.quote: paraphrase: 22-24 January 1943; more than 6,000 arrested and 40,000 identities checked; about 20,000 displaced (infobox); about 1,500 buildings destroyed (citation needed in source)

S8.title: INA, La demolition du quartier du vieux port (web-search snippet only: host not fetchable)
S8.quote: paraphrase from search snippet: demolition started on 1 February and ran until 17 February 1943; about 1,400 buildings demolished

S9.title: Wikipedia EN, Hotel de Ville, Marseille
S9.quote: Work began in 1653 (foundation stone 25 October), completed in September 1673; in early 1943 one of only four buildings to survive in the surrounding area

S10.title: Wikipedia EN, La Vieille Charite
S10.quote: Building began in 1671 and was completed in 1749; architect Pierre Puget; central chapel 1679-1704

S11.title: Wikipedia EN, St. Victor's Abbey, Marseille
S11.quote: c. 415 John Cassian founded the abbey; 1020 construction of the upper church begun; 1040 church dedicated by Pope Benedict IX; 1361-62 Guillaume Grimoard abbot then Pope Urban V encloses the abbey with high crenellated walls

S12.title: Wikipedia EN, Marseille Cathedral
S12.quote: old cathedral 12th century; Napoleon III laid the foundation stone in 1852 of the new cathedral; first service 1893; completion 1896; consecration 1897; architects Leon Vaudoyer and Henri-Jacques Esperandieu

S13.title: Wikipedia EN, Notre-Dame de la Garde
S13.quote: chapel begun in 1214; Francis I fort 1536; present basilica first stone 11 September 1853, consecrated 1864 (still unfinished), statue dedicated 24 September 1870

S14.title: Wikipedia FR, Rue de la Republique (Marseille)
S14.quote: paraphrase: council adopted the project in November 1858; percement begun in 1862; inaugurated 1864; 1,100 m; 935 houses destroyed and 61 streets partly or fully removed; called rue Imperiale, renamed rue de la Republique on 16 October 1870

S15.title: Wikipedia FR, Cite radieuse de Marseille
S15.quote: paraphrase: construction October 1947 to October 1952; first stone 14 October 1947; inaugurated 14 October 1952; 56 m high, 137 m long, 24 m wide

S16.title: Wikipedia EN, Euromediterranee
S16.quote: paraphrase: began in 1995 under Mayor Robert Vigouroux and the State; original area 310 hectares; Act 2 from 2007 added 170 hectares; includes MuCEM, Villa Mediterranee, Docks renovation, CMA CGM Tower

S17.title: Wikipedia EN, CMA CGM Tower
S17.quote: paraphrase: construction July 2006, completion September 2011, about 147 m, architect Zaha Hadid

S18.title: Wikipedia EN, Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations
S18.quote: paraphrase: opened in 2013 as part of Marseille-Provence 2013; architect Rudy Ricciotti with Roland Carta; 130 m footbridge to Fort Saint-Jean

S19.title: Wikipedia EN, Marseille Transporter Bridge
S19.quote: inaugurated on 15 December 1905; on 22 August 1944 the German military blew it up, only the north tower fell; the rest collapsed on 1 September 1945

S20.title: Wikipedia FR, Fernand Pouillon
S20.quote: paraphrase: reconstruction of the Vieux-Port listed as 1947-1953, project could start in 1949; modern buildings on both sides of the hotel de ville were built by Pouillon

S21.title: Wikipedia FR, Histoire de Marseille
S21.quote: paraphrase: vicomtes from the mid-10th century; 1252 peace with Charles d'Anjou; King Rene's tower 1447-1453 built on the ruins of the Maubert tower; Fort Saint-Jean built in the 17th century on Louis XIV's orders; plague of 1720: about 38,000 deaths out of 75,000 inhabitants

S23.title: Jardin des Vestiges (Wikipedia mirror, garbled) + academic survey summaries via web search
S23.quote: paraphrase, low confidence: first rampart end of 5th c. BC (white limestone base, clay brick); rebuilt probably second half of 4th c. BC; rebuilt on a large scale in the second half of the 2nd c. BC; archaic city about 20 ha on the Saint-Laurent, Moulins and Roquette hills; the ancient city included the Saint-Laurent, Moulins and Carmes hills

S24.title: Sites Vauban, Marseille (web-search summary)
S24.quote: paraphrase: 1665 king orders an arsenal for the galleys; 1666 extension decided by Louis XIV; 1672 earlier ramparts razed; 1694 new enceinte; arsenal closed 1748, demolished in the 1780s (Marseille Tourisme)

S25.title: Marseille Tourisme / Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur, La Joliette and the Docks (web-search summaries)
S25.quote: paraphrase: Joliette basin authorized 1844, completed 1853; Docks 1858-1863/64/66 depending on source; Gare Saint-Charles opened 1848

S26.title: Catholic Encyclopedia, Marseilles (web-search summary)
S26.quote: paraphrase: Visigothic 476, Ostrogothic 507, Frankish from 536 (other sources 508 and 537); in feudal times the city was divided among the bishop, the viscount and the abbey of Saint-Victor

S27.title: Wikipedia EN, Siege of Marseille (1524)
S27.quote: paraphrase: August and September 1524, Italian War; besiegers withdrew under the threat of a French relief army led by Francis I

S28.title: BnF Gallica, Stadtplan von Marseille, Sonderausgabe 6.40 (Generalstab des Heeres, 1940)
S28.quote: 1:10,000 plan georeferenced in cities/marseille/mappe/FONTI_MAPPE.md; 347 test blocks in saintjean_isolati_test_1940.geojson (not a full survey, not used as geometry: the pre-1943 quarter in the render is approximated from the plan)

S29.title: BDNB (CSTB), data_marseille/buildings.json
S29.quote: year of construction per building group; share without year inside 1.5 km of the Vieux-Port: 17.6% (misure_bdnb.json)

S30.title: Wikipedia EN, standard dates of French regimes (not re-fetched, from general knowledge)
S30.quote: paraphrase: First Republic Sept 1792; Empire 1804; Restoration 1814; July Monarchy 1830; Second Republic 1848; Second Empire Dec 1852; Third Republic Sept 1870; Vichy 10 July 1940; GPRF 1944; Fourth Republic Oct 1946; Fifth Republic Oct 1958

S31.title: Inventaire general du patrimoine, bassin de la Grande-Joliette and port works (web-search snippets only: pop.culture.gouv.fr and ehne.fr not reachable)
S31.quote: paraphrase from search snippets: law of 5 August 1844 orders the Joliette basin; infrastructure in use from 1847; Joliette completed as an auxiliary port in 1853; law of 10 June 1854 for the Lazaret basin; decree of 23 November 1856 for the Lazaret and Arenc basins; construction of the Arenc basin began in November 1856; Lazaret and Arenc moles built 1856-1864; Napoleon basin 1859; Digue du Large completed in 1925 (tourisme-marseille); no date found for the Bassin National

S32.title: Wikipedia FR, Pont transbordeur de Marseille
S32.quote: paraphrase: links the quais du Port and de Rive Neuve; deck 239 m between two pylons, 52 m above the sea; pylons 86.60 m; built in 19 months, inaugurated 15 December 1905; north pylon fell 22 August 1944; rest collapsed 1 September 1945

zones.name: Archaic Massalia (Saint-Laurent and Moulins hills)
zones.note: Phocaean city founded c. 600 BC on the hills north of the Lacydon; about 20 ha for the archaic phase (S23, low). Polygon is a hand sketch around the Moulins/Saint-Laurent buttes (Vieille Charite area), +-150 m, NOT surveyed.

zones.name: Hellenistic Massalia (Saint-Laurent, Moulins and Carmes hills)
zones.note: Greek and Roman city (about 50 ha, 4th c. BC peak ~50,000 people per S1) extending east to the Carmes hill and the Jardin des Vestiges. Hand sketch, +-150 m. The Lacydon inlet reached the Bourse/Jardin des Vestiges area: shoreline NOT modelled (no history.water).

zones.name: Saint-Victor and the south shore
zones.note: Abbey founded c. 415 (S11); a bourg grows around it. Hand sketch around the Saint-Victor abbey (Wikipedia coordinates 43.2903, 5.3656).

zones.name: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)
zones.note: North shore of the Vieux-Port inside the medieval walls, whose exact line is NOT verified. Hand sketch.

zones.name: Louis XIV extension (1666-1700)
zones.note: First growth beyond the medieval ramparts: Cours Belsunce, Canebiere, Rue Paradis area. S24: 1666 extension decided; 1694 new enceinte (sources disagree on whether the area doubled or tripled). Hand sketch of the quarter, not of the 1694 wall line.

zones.name: Joliette new quarter (1844-1870)
zones.note: Land behind the Joliette basin (authorized 1844, completed 1853, S25) and the Docks (1858-1863/66). The basin itself and the reclaimed quays are NOT modelled (no land phases): they appear with the modern coastline from the first frame unless land.json is dated.

walls.name: Ramparts of Massalia and medieval Marseille (approximate line)
walls.note: First rampart end of 5th c. BC, rebuilt 4th c. BC and large-scale in 2nd c. BC (S23, low). Razed 1672 (S24, low). One ring is a simplification: the medieval line is not verified.

gutting.name: Rue Imperiale (Rue de la Republique)
gutting.note: Percement begun 1862, inaugurated 1864, 1,100 m, 935 houses destroyed (S14). Round 2: centerline shifted ~45 m east at the Joliette end so that it passes through the wide corridor flagged by QA at (43.30428, 5.36665); still a 2-point estimate (+-40 m): replace with the OSM way of Rue de la Republique (Overpass not reachable from the sandbox).

fires.name: Siege of Massilia 49 BC
fires.note: 19 April-6 September 49 BC = -49 + 0.30 .. -49 + 0.68 (S3). The attack side is NOT identified in the sources read: polygon is the western part of the Hellenistic city, no building destroyed.

fires.name: Saint-Jean quarter 1943
fires.note: Dynamiting 1 Feb (1943.088) to 17 Feb (1943.132): start S6, end S8 (INA snippet, not fetched). Ring = ~14.8 ha box between Fort Saint-Jean and the Hotel de Ville, quay to about 200 m north: hand sketch, validated only against the 347 test blocks (see NOTE_STORIA.md). Wave from the fort side (origin) eastward. rebuild_years 7 puts new current buildings at ~1950-1954 (Pouillon from 1949, S20; district finished 1956, S6).

bridges.name: Transporter Bridge (Old Port)
bridges.note: Inaugurated 15 Dec 1905; blown up 22 Aug 1944 (north tower fell); rest collapsed 1 Sep 1945 (S19). Round 2: centre moved to the OSM node 'Pont Transbordeur' (43.292385, 5.364884, data_marseille/landmarks_osm.json), which is near the harbour mouth, not at the Hotel de Ville as in round 1 (error). Round 4: `d` = 1944.64 (22 Aug 1944, the sabotage; the kit has one deck per bridge and no partial collapse, so the ruin standing until 1 Sep 1945 is NOT shown: limit). Span 239 m between the quais du Port and de Rive Neuve (fr:Pont transbordeur de Marseille, [Certain]); N-S orientation is [Guessing].

landmarks.name: Abbey of Saint-Victor
landmarks.note: Upper church begun 1020, dedicated 1040 (S11). Fortification by Urban V 1361-62 not modelled. Coordinates = Wikipedia.

landmarks.name: King Rene's Tower
landmarks.note: Built 1447-1453 on the ruins of the Maubert tower (S21). Position at the south-east corner of Fort Saint-Jean from memory, +-60 m.

landmarks.name: Fort Saint-Jean
landmarks.note: Forts built from 1660 on Louis XIV's orders (S2, S21); end year 1668 is a Likely guess (S21 gives only '17th century'). Footprint from memory.

landmarks.name: Fort Saint-Nicolas
landmarks.note: Built from 1660 (S2); 1664 end is a Likely guess. Coordinates from the QA control point of the 1940 map (OSM centroid, +-45 m).

landmarks.name: Hotel de Ville
landmarks.note: Work began 1653, completed September 1673; survived the 1943 destruction (S9). Position from memory (+-80 m): footprint auto may miss.

landmarks.name: La Vieille Charite
landmarks.note: Built 1671-1749 by Pierre Puget and successors; Wikipedia coordinates 43.3003, 5.3678 (S10).

landmarks.name: Marseille Cathedral (Major)
landmarks.note: Foundation stone 1852, first service 1893, completed 1896, consecrated 1897 (S12). Old Major (12th c.) not modelled separately. Coordinates = Wikipedia.

landmarks.name: Gare Saint-Charles
landmarks.note: Station opened 1848 (S2, S25); work start 1845 is a guess. Coordinates = Wikipedia.

landmarks.name: Notre-Dame de la Garde
landmarks.note: First stone 11 Sept 1853, consecrated 1864, statue 24 Sept 1870 (S13). Modelled as the tower only; coordinates = Wikipedia.

landmarks.name: Stade Velodrome
landmarks.note: Opened 1937 (S2); start year 1935 is a guess. Coordinates = Wikipedia. Not a stop (far from the centre).

landmarks.name: Cite Radieuse
landmarks.note: First stone 14 Oct 1947, inaugurated 14 Oct 1952, 56 x 137 x 24 m (S15). Position from memory (+-100 m): footprint auto may miss, params give the slab.

landmarks.name: CMA CGM Tower
landmarks.note: July 2006 to September 2011, about 147 m (S17). Position from memory (+-100 m).

landmarks.name: MuCEM
landmarks.note: Opened in 2013 (S18); construction start 2010.0 is a guess and the exact opening date (7 June 2013, [Likely]) is not in the page read. Position from memory (+-80 m).

title: MARSEILLE
600 BC TO NOW

cards.title: A colony on the Lacydon
lines: Greeks from Phocaea, in Asia Minor, found Massalia around 600 BC.
The settlers choose the hills north of a sheltered inlet, the Lacydon.

cards.title: A second wave
lines: After the Persians destroy Phocaea, new colonists arrive around 540 BC.

cards.title: Walls of limestone and clay
lines: A first rampart rises in the late 5th century BC.
It is rebuilt in the 4th century and on a large scale in the 2nd.
cards.target: Hellenistic Massalia (Saint-Laurent, Moulins and Carmes hills)
cards.note: S23 is a mirror plus search summaries: verify rampart dates in the excavation literature before print.

cards.title: Pytheas sails north
lines: The Massaliote navigator Pytheas explores the Atlantic coasts, around 330-320 BC.
cards.target: Hellenistic Massalia (Saint-Laurent, Moulins and Carmes hills)

cards.title: Rome comes to the rescue
lines: Gallic tribes threaten the city in 123-121 BC; Roman armies drive them back.
The alliance with Rome grows closer.
cards.target: Hellenistic Massalia (Saint-Laurent, Moulins and Carmes hills)

cards.title: A city that backed the wrong side
lines: After Caesar's siege the city keeps nominal autonomy but loses its trading empire.
cards.target: Hellenistic Massalia (Saint-Laurent, Moulins and Carmes hills)

cards.title: Christians in the Roman port
lines: Christianity appears in Roman Massilia; catacombs above the harbor mark an early community.

cards.title: The martyr Victor
lines: Around 290 Victor is martyred in Marseille; the abbey of Saint-Victor will take his name.

cards.title: Cassian and Saint-Victor
lines: Tradition says the monk John Cassian founds two monasteries at Saint-Victor around 415.
Archaeology finds nothing there before the late 5th century.

cards.title: The Goths arrive
lines: Visigoth forces under King Euric take Marseille around 470.
Franks follow in 536 (some sources say 537).

cards.title: Charles Martel sacks the city
lines: Arab forces invited into Provence are driven out in 739 as the Franks sack Marseille.
cards.target: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)

cards.title: Raiders from the sea
lines: Saracens sack Marseille in 839.
cards.target: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)

cards.title: Three lords, one city
lines: In feudal times the city is split between the bishop, the viscount and the abbey of Saint-Victor.
cards.target: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)

cards.title: A commune and a chapel
lines: Marseille governs itself as a commune from the early 13th century (sources differ: 1212-18).
In 1214 a priest begins a chapel on the Garde hill.
cards.target: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)

cards.title: Anjou takes Marseille
lines: Charles of Anjou, count of Provence since 1246, takes the city in 1252.
A revolt is crushed in 1262-63.
cards.target: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)

cards.title: The Black Death
lines: Plague kills about 15,000 of 25,000 inhabitants.
cards.target: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)

cards.title: The Aragonese sack the port
lines: Alfonso V of Aragon sacks the city on 20 November 1423.
cards.target: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)

cards.title: Provence joins France
lines: Charles III dies in December 1481 and leaves Provence to Louis XI.
The union is confirmed in 1486.
cards.target: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)

cards.title: A siege lifted
lines: Imperial troops besiege the city in August-September 1524.
They withdraw as Francis I marches to its relief.
cards.target: Medieval Marseille (Ville haute and Ville basse)

cards.title: The king enters through a breach
lines: Louis XIV subdues a rebellious Marseille in 1660.
Forts Saint-Jean and Saint-Nicolas are built to watch the city.

cards.title: A new city beyond the walls
lines: In 1666 the king decides to enlarge Marseille; the old ramparts are razed in 1672 and a new wall follows in 1694.
A galley arsenal fills the port from 1665.
cards.note: S24 is a web-search summary: verify 1672 and 1694.

cards.title: The Great Plague
lines: A ship from the Levant brings plague in 1720.
About 38,000 of 75,000 inhabitants die.

cards.title: The song of the Marseillais
lines: Volunteers march from Marseille to Paris in 1792; their song becomes La Marseillaise.

cards.title: The city without a name
lines: After a federalist revolt, Marseille is renamed Ville-sans-nom in 1793.
cards.note: Some sources give 1794 for the renaming.

cards.title: A new port for steam
lines: The Joliette basin is authorized in 1844 and completed in 1853.
The Old Port is no longer enough.

cards.title: Water for a growing city
lines: The Canal de Marseille opens in 1849.

cards.title: The Docks of the Joliette
lines: Giant warehouses rise from 1858; completion dates range from 1863 to 1866.
The Arenc basin was begun in November 1856.

cards.title: Suez opens
lines: The Suez Canal opens in 1869 and boosts the port; the Palais Longchamp is completed the same year.

cards.title: A street changes its name
lines: On 16 October 1870 the Rue Imperiale becomes the Rue de la Republique.

cards.title: Horse-drawn trams
lines: Horse-drawn trams begin to run in 1876.

cards.title: Cholera
lines: A cholera epidemic strikes the city in 1884.

cards.title: 2,500 years
lines: Marseille celebrates the 2,500th anniversary of its founding in 1899.
Olympique de Marseille is formed the same year.

cards.title: Plague returns
lines: Bubonic plague breaks out again in September 1903.

cards.title: The colonial exhibition
lines: Marseille hosts colonial exhibitions in 1906 and 1922.

cards.title: The Grand Theatre burns
lines: The Grand Theatre burns down on 13 November 1919.

cards.title: An airport and a second exhibition
lines: Marseille Provence Airport opens in 1922, the year of a second colonial exhibition.

cards.title: Assassination on the quay
lines: King Alexander I of Yugoslavia and French minister Louis Barthou are assassinated on 9 October 1934.

cards.title: A stadium for the city
lines: The Stade Velodrome opens in 1937.

cards.title: Vichy and the bombs
lines: In June 1940 German and Italian aircraft bomb Marseille.
The city then lies in the unoccupied zone, under the Vichy regime.
cards.note: 'Unoccupied zone' is general knowledge, not read in the cited pages [Likely].

cards.title: German troops occupy the city
lines: In November 1942 German forces occupy Marseille.

cards.title: The Saint-Jean quarter is condemned
lines: On 22-24 January 1943 a police roundup arrests more than 6,000 people and expels about 20,000.
From 1 February about 1,500 buildings on 14 hectares are dynamited. The model is a partial reconstruction.
cards.note: Counts vary by source: 1,400-1,500 buildings; 20,000-30,000 expelled. The pre-1943 houses shown in the render: about 60% of the footprint follows the 1940 German plan block outlines (45 blocks, BnF Gallica), extruded; the rest is generated fill; heights and construction dates are estimated (round 5, yb-modeler: hist_blocks.json). Say 'block outlines follow the plan, buildings are estimated', never 'follows the plan' without the reservation, in the description. Round 3: card moved before the hover (y 1943.02, 'condemned') so that the 9 s hover has no card text (cold open window clean).

cards.title: Liberation and a fallen bridge
lines: Marseille is liberated in late August 1944; the Germans blow up the Transporter Bridge on 22 August.
The last standing parts collapse on 1 September 1945.

cards.title: Rebuilding the Old Port
lines: From 1949 the architect Fernand Pouillon builds new stone blocks on both sides of the Hotel de Ville.
The district is finished by 1956; the old lanes do not return.
cards.note: Pouillon works list 1947-53 (S20); fr:Rafle de Marseille says reconstruction finished 1956. 'The old lanes do not return' is an inference from the blocks, mark Likely.

cards.title: Le Corbusier's Radiant City
lines: The Cite Radieuse is inaugurated on 14 October 1952: a 56-meter slab of apartments after five years of work.

cards.title: The pieds-noirs
lines: After Algerian independence in 1962 about 150,000 pieds-noirs settle in Marseille.

cards.title: A tunnel under the Old Port
lines: The Old Port tunnel opens in 1967.

cards.title: Metro and a shipping giant
lines: The first metro line opens in 1977.
The shipping company CMA CGM is founded the same year.

cards.title: The TGV arrives
lines: The TGV Sud-Est begins serving Marseille in 1983.

cards.title: Euromediterranee
lines: In 1995 the state and the city launch Euromediterranee: 310 hectares around La Joliette.
An extension adds 170 hectares from 2007.

cards.title: 2,600 years
lines: The Parc du 26e Centenaire opens in 2001, marking 2,600 years since the founding.

cards.title: Tramway and a bigger waterfront
lines: The first tramway line opens in 2007.
Euromediterranee adds 170 hectares to the north.

cards.title: A tower for a shipping giant
lines: Zaha Hadid's 147-meter CMA CGM Tower is completed in September 2011.
